mcqs.question: A common examiner point on "Incomplete dominance and codominance" is that a statement is only valid when its condition of applicability is met. Is that TRUE or FALSE?
mcqs.explanation: Every NEB rule has a scope (e.g. a specific range, temperature, or sign convention); stating the condition earns full marks.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Incomplete dominance: heterozygote is INTERMEDIATE (red × white snapdragon → pink); F2 = 1:2:1 both genotypic and phenotypic — the ratio change from 3:1 is the mark.
Trick 2: Codominance: BOTH alleles express fully (AB blood group: IA and IB codominant; i is recessive) — no blending, both products appear.
Trick 3: Blood group genotypes: A = IAIA or IAi; B = IBIB or IBi; AB = IAIB; O = ii — the table for the 2-mark question.
Trick 4: Distinguish in one phrase: incomplete = blended phenotype; codominance = both phenotypes side by side.
